title: Jurisdiction based on property
summary: Property-based jurisdiction uses a defendant’s interests in property as part of the basis for adjudication. The course distinguishes disputes about the property itself from efforts to use unrelated property to obtain leverage over a person.
notes: The presence of property can be important to contacts and to the claim. The rule does not mean property is irrelevant; it rejects the automatic sufficiency of the unrelated property basis used in Shaffer.

sections.Meaning: Property-based jurisdiction uses a defendant’s interests in property as part of the basis for adjudication. The course distinguishes disputes about the property itself from efforts to use unrelated property to obtain leverage over a person.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the property, its location, the claim’s connection to it, and how it was brought under the court’s control. Shaffer requires consideration of the defendant’s forum contacts rather than treating an artificial statutory location of shares as automatically sufficient.
